children: Georgia’s trade deficit narrowed to USD 809.9 million in August 2026 from USD 894.4 million in the same month last year, marking the smallest trade shortfall since January.
Outbound shipments climbed 24.8% year-on-year to USD 752.4 million, while imports increased at a much slower pace of 4.3% to a four-month low of USD 1,562.2 million.
During the January–August period, exports surged 22.1% to USD 5,422.5 million, primarily driven by petroleum and petroleum oils (1,067.7%) and precious metal ores and concentrates (68.6%).
Export growth was particularly strong to China (177.3%) and Russia (4.1%).
Meanwhile, imports rose 3.4% to USD 12,504.4 million, supported by higher purchases of petroleum and petroleum oils (37.4%), despite a decline in imports of motor cars (-12.5%).
Imports recorded the largest increases from Russia (24.9%) and China (22.1%).
Georgia’s trade deficit for the January–August period narrowed to USD 7,081.9 million from USD 7,650.7 million in the same period of 2025.

title: Georgia Trade Deficit Smallest in 7 Months
